# I. Bayesian multi-level survival analysis for type (combined) with random intercept for centre
Use Bayes theorum to combine the evidence from these two studies to inform the prior for the effect of type B and AB on survival in our model, and then use the data from our study to update this prior to get a posterior distribution for the effect of type B and AB on survival in our population.


## Set prior for beta variables
Set an informative prior...
 ~ student_t(df = 3, location = 1.292032, scale = 0.3219278)


#### i. Prior for beta of type
```{r}
prior_beta_type <- student_t(df = 3, location = 1.292032, scale = 0.3219278, autoscale = FALSE)
```





## Fit model
NB use status ... rstanarm requires the dead animals to be classified as 1, whilst censored are 0.
```{r}
mod_type <- stan_surv(formula = Surv(time, status) ~ type
                      + (1| centre),
  data = df,
  prior_intercept = normal(location = 0, scale = 20, autoscale = FALSE),
  prior = prior_beta_type,
  prior_covariance =  decov(regularization = 2, concentration = 1, shape = 1, scale = 1),
  iter    = 10000,
  chains = 4,
  cores = 4,
  adapt_delta = 0.9999,  # Often helpful for complex models
  seed = 666)
```



## Summarise priors from model
```{r}
prior_summary(mod_type)
```



## Model summary
```{r}
summary(mod_type)
```



## Model short summary
```{r}

```

```{r}

```

### 3. Check prosterior vs prior for beta variable
#### a. extract draws for posterior and prior
```{r}
# extract draws
post_draws  <- as.matrix(mod_type)
prior_draws <- as.matrix(mod_type_prior_only)
```



#### b. type_ab
##### i. plot marginal distributions for posterior and prior
``` {r}
# Compare marginal distributions
dens(post_draws[, "typeab"], show.zero = TRUE, col = "red", main = "Informed prior vs posterior for type AB", xlab = "Beta coefficient for effect of type AB", xlim = c(-2, 3), ylim = c(0, 1.4) ) 
dens(prior_draws[, "typeab"], add=TRUE, col = "blue", show.zero = TRUE)
```




##### ii. compute prior tail probability of posterior mean
If this probability is very small (e.g. < 0.05), the posterior lies in a region the prior considered implausible.
```{r}
beta_hat <- mean(post_draws[, "typeab"])

mean(abs(prior_draws[, "typeab"] - beta_hat) <
       abs(prior_draws[, "typeab"] - mean(prior_draws[, "typeab"])))

```






#### b. type_b
##### i. plot marginal distributions for posterior and prior
```{r}
# Compare marginal distributions
dens(post_draws[, "typeb"], show.zero = TRUE, col = "red", main = "Informed prior vs posterior for type B",
     xlab = "Beta coefficient for effect of type B", xlim = c(-2, 3), ylim = c(0, 1.4) )
dens(prior_draws[, "typeb"], add=TRUE, col = "blue", show.zero = TRUE)
```




##### ii. compute prior tail probability of posterior mean
If this probability is very small (e.g. < 0.05), the posterior lies in a region the prior considered implausible.
```{r}
beta_hat <- mean(post_draws[, "typeb"])

mean(abs(prior_draws[, "typeb"] - beta_hat) <
       abs(prior_draws[, "typeb"] - mean(prior_draws[, "typeb"])))

```



### 4. Sensitivity analyses to assess robustness of results to choice of prior
#### a. create priors of different strength for type variable
To determine whether the substantive conclusions depend upon the exact prior choice.
Given such a small scale, best to adjust the strong prior is based on the combined estimate from the literature, whilst moderate and weak priors are then scaled up from the strong prior.  These latter priors ensure that the data are not overwhelmed by the prior, but still allow for some regularisation to improve model convergence and reduce overfitting.
Therefore, strong prior should be 1x the combine scale, then increase this by 2x for moderate and 4x for weak..
```{r}
priors_bin <- list(
  weak = student_t(df = 3, location = 1.292032, scale = 1.2877111, autoscale = FALSE),
  moderate = student_t(df = 3, location = 1.292032, scale = 0.6438556, autoscale = FALSE),
  strong = student_t(df = 3, location = 1.292032, scale = 0.3219278, autoscale = FALSE)
)
```

Set an informative, weakly-regularising prior...
 ~ student_t(df = 3, location = 1.29611, scale = 0.3244759)

         suggested scale
strong         0.3219278
moderate       0.6438556
weak           1.2877111


#### b. refit model with different priors and compare results
```{r}
fits <- lapply(priors_bin, function(p) {
  stan_surv(formula = Surv(time, status) ~ type 
            + (1| centre),
            basehaz = "ms",
            data = df,
            prior_intercept = normal(location = 0, scale = 5, autoscale = FALSE),
            prior = p,
            prior_covariance =  decov(regularization = 2, concentration = 1, shape = 1, scale = 1),
            iter    = 2000,
            chains = 4,
            cores = 4,
            adapt_delta = 0.9999,  # Often helpful for complex models
            seed = 666
            )
})
```



#### c. compare posterior intervals for hazard ratios for type_ab across different priors
##### i. type_ab
```{r}
# calculate median hazard ratio for type_ab across different priors
HR_med_sens <- sapply(fits, function(f) {
  posterior::as_draws_df(f) |>
    as.data.frame() |>
    summarise(
      median = exp(quantile(typeab, probs = 0.5))
    )
})
HR_med <- c(HR_med_sens[[1]], HR_med_sens[[2]], HR_med_sens[[3]])


# calculate 89% credible interval for hazard ratio for type_ab across different priors
HR_sens <- sapply(fits, function(f) {
  exp(posterior_interval(f, pars = "typeab", prob = 0.89))
})

# combine median and credible intervals into a summary table
HR_sens_summary <- rbind(HR_med, HR_sens)
row.names(HR_sens_summary) <- c("Median", "Lower", "Upper")

# transpose the table for better readability
HR_sens_summary
```







##### ii. type_b
```{r}
# calculate median hazard ratio for type_ab across different priors
HR_med_sens <- sapply(fits, function(f) {
  posterior::as_draws_df(f) |>
    as.data.frame() |>
    summarise(
      median = exp(quantile(typeb, probs = 0.5))
    )
})
HR_med <- c(HR_med_sens[[1]], HR_med_sens[[2]], HR_med_sens[[3]])


# calculate 89% credible interval for hazard ratio for type_ab across different priors
HR_sens <- sapply(fits, function(f) {
  exp(posterior_interval(f, pars = "typeb", prob = 0.89))
})

# combine median and credible intervals into a summary table
HR_sens_summary <- rbind(HR_med, HR_sens)
row.names(HR_sens_summary) <- c("Median", "Lower", "Upper")

# transpose the table for better readability
HR_sens_summary
```



Text for paper:
"Prior–likelihood compatibility was assessed using prior predictive checks and by comparing prior and posterior marginal distributions of key parameters. Sensitivity analyses were performed by refitting models under weaker and stronger priors; substantive conclusions were robust to these choices.”

```{r}
head(ps)
```




#### 3. Plot
```{r}
panel_labels <- c('1' = "Type A", '2' = "Type B", '3' = "Type AB")
pps <- plot(ps) +
  aes(colour = factor(id), fill = factor(id)) +
  theme(legend.position = "none") +
  facet_wrap(~ id, labeller = labeller(id = panel_labels)) +
           theme(axis.title.y = element_text(size=12, face="bold"), 
               axis.title.x = element_text(size=12, face="bold"),
               title = element_text(size=12, face="bold"),
               plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5),
               axis.text.x = element_text(color = "grey50", size = 10),
               axis.text.y = element_text(color = "grey50",size = 10)) +
            theme(strip.text.x = element_text(size = 10, face = "bold.italic"),
                   strip.background = element_rect(fill="white")
        )
print(pps)
```

# II. Bayesian multi-level survival analysis for s_age with random intercept for centre

## Set prior for beta variables
Set an informative prior...
 ~ student_t(df = 3, location = 0.1731489, scale = 0.1596095)

```{r}
prior_beta_age <- student_t(df = 3, location = 0.1731489, scale = 0.1596095, autoscale = FALSE)
```




## Fit model with for s_age
NB use status ... rstanarm requires the dead animals to be classified as 1, whilst censored are 0.
```{r}
mod_age <- stan_surv(formula = Surv(time, status) ~ s_age
                     + (1| centre),
  data = df,
  basehaz = "ms",
  prior_intercept = normal(location = 0, scale = 22, autoscale = FALSE),
  prior = prior_beta_age,
  prior_covariance =  decov(regularization = 2, concentration = 1, shape = 1, scale = 1),
  iter    = 10000,
  chains = 4,
  cores = 4,
  adapt_delta = 0.999,  # Often helpful for complex models
  seed = 666)
```




## Summarise priors from model
```{r}
prior_summary(mod_age)
```



## Model summary
```{r}
summary(mod_age)
```



## Model short summary... shows estimates of coefficients
```{r}

```





##  Plot Baseline hazard of model
```{r}

```



## Plots of model convergences


#### c. compute prior tail probability of posterior mean

### 4. Sensitivity analyses to assess robustness of results to choice of prior
#### a. create priors of different strength for s_age variable
To determine whether the substantive conclusions depend upon the exact prior choice.

NB the scale variable is strengthened or weakened by multiplying or dividing the scale of the main prior by 2, respectively. The location is set to the posterior mean from the main model, to ensure that the priors are centred on a plausible value.
```{r}
priors_bin <- list(
  weak = student_t(df = 3, location = 0.1731489, scale = 0.6384379, autoscale = FALSE),
  moderate = student_t(df = 3, location = 0.1731489, scale = 0.3192190, autoscale = FALSE),
  strong = student_t(df = 3, location = 0.1731489, scale = 0.1596095, autoscale = FALSE)
)
```

Set an informative, regularising prior...
 ~ student_t(df = 3, location = 0.3086223, scale = 0.1497119)
NB set at 0.5 given that ther scale is so small, to ensure that the data are not overwhelmed by the prior, but still allow for some regularisation to improve model convergence and reduce overfitting.

strong         0.1596095
moderate       0.3192190
weak           0.6384379



#### b. refit model with different priors and compare results
```{r}
fits <- lapply(priors_bin, function(p) {
  stan_surv(formula = Surv(time, status) ~ s_age
            + (1| centre),
            basehaz = "ms",
            data = df,
            prior_intercept = normal(location = 0, scale = 20, autoscale = FALSE),
            prior = p,
            prior_covariance =  decov(regularization = 2, concentration = 1, shape = 1, scale = 1),
            iter    = 2000,
            chains = 4,
            cores = 4,
            adapt_delta = 0.9999,  # Often helpful for complex models
            seed = 666
            )
})
```



#### c. compare posterior intervals for hazard ratios for type_ab across different priors
```{r}
# calculate median hazard ratio across different priors
HR_med_sens <- sapply(fits, function(f) {
  posterior::as_draws_df(f) |>
    as.data.frame() |>
    summarise(
      median = exp(quantile(s_age, probs = 0.5))
    )
})
HR_med <- c(HR_med_sens[[1]], HR_med_sens[[2]], HR_med_sens[[3]])


# calculate 89% credible interval for hazard ratio across different priors
HR_sens <- sapply(fits, function(f) {
  exp(posterior_interval(f, pars = "s_age", prob = 0.89))
})

# combine median and credible intervals into a summary table
HR_sens_summary <- rbind(HR_med, HR_sens)
row.names(HR_sens_summary) <- c("Median", "Lower", "Upper")

# transpose the table for better readability
HR_sens_summary
```

# III. Bayesian multi-level survival analysis for EFFECT OF SURGERY (surgery y/n) with random intercept for centre


## Set prior for beta variables
Set an informative prior...
 ~ student_t(df = 3, location = -0.879165, scale = 0.2911939)
 
```{r}
prior_beta_sx <- student_t(df = 3, location = c(-0.879165, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0),
                           scale = c(0.29119395, 2, 2, 2, 2, 2, 2),
                           autoscale = c(FALSE, TRUE, FALSE, FALSE, FALSE, FALSE, TRUE))
```
NB needed to set a tighter scale variable for prior_intercept and also prior_beta_sx in order to improve regularisation and resolve divergent transitions.

Based on the DAG, use the following adjustment variables: age, clin signs, concurrent congen, pressure grad, referral centre, stenosis type.




## Fit model with for surgery (plus correction set)
NB use status ... rstanarm requires the dead animals to be classified as 1, whilst censored are 0.
```{r}
mod_sx <- stan_surv(formula = Surv(time, status) ~ surgery
                    + s_age
                    + concurrent_congenital
                    + type
                    + clinical_signs
                    + s_pv_max_pg
                    + (1| centre),
  data = df,
  basehaz = "ms",
  prior_intercept = normal(location = 0, scale = 10, autoscale = FALSE),
  prior = prior_beta_sx,
  prior_covariance =  decov(regularization = 2, concentration = 1, shape = 1, scale = 1),
  iter    = 10000,
  chains = 4,
  cores = 4,
  adapt_delta = 0.9999,  # Often helpful for complex models
  seed = 666)
```

### 1. Check performance of posterior probability





### 2. Check performance of prior probability
```{r}

ps_check(mod_pg_prior_only) |>
  suppressWarnings()
```




### 3. Check prosterior vs prior for beta variable
#### a. extract draws for posterior and prior
```{r}
# extract draws
post_draws  <- as.matrix(mod_pg)
prior_draws <- as.matrix(mod_pg_prior_only)
```



#### b. plot marginal distributions for posterior and prior
``` {r}
# Compare marginal distributions
dens(post_draws[, "s_pv_max_pg"], show.zero = TRUE, col = "red", main = "Informed prior vs posterior for PVmax PG", xlab = "Beta coefficient for effect of PVmax PG",, xlim = c(-0.5, 1.5), ylim = c(0, 3.0)) 
dens(prior_draws[, "s_pv_max_pg"], add=TRUE, col = "blue", show.zero = TRUE)
```





#### c. compute prior tail probability of posterior mean
If this probability is very small (e.g. < 0.05), the posterior lies in a region the prior considered implausible.
```{r}
beta_hat <- mean(post_draws[, "s_pv_max_pg"])

mean(abs(prior_draws[, "s_pv_max_pg"] - beta_hat) <
       abs(prior_draws[, "s_pv_max_pg"] - mean(prior_draws[, "s_pv_max_pg"])))

```





### 4. Sensitivity analyses to assess robustness of results to choice of prior
#### a. create priors of different strength for s_pv_max_pg variable
To determine whether the substantive conclusions depend upon the exact prior choice.

NB the scale variable is strengthened or weakened by multiplying or dividing the scale of the main prior by 2, respectively. The location is set to the posterior mean from the main model, to ensure that the priors are centred on a plausible value.
```{r}
priors_bin <- list(
  weak = student_t(df = 3, location = 0.687753, scale = (0.5840526), autoscale = FALSE),
  moderate = student_t(df = 3, location = 0.687753, scale = (0.2920263), autoscale = FALSE),
  strong = student_t(df = 3, location = 0.687753, scale = (0.1460131), autoscale = FALSE)
)
```

Set an informative, regularising prior...
 ~ student_t(df = 3, location = 0.687753, scale = 0.1460131)
NB set at 0.5 given that ther scale is so small, to ensure that the data are not overwhelmed by the prior, but still allow for some regularisation to improve model convergence and reduce overfitting.

strong         0.1460131
moderate       0.2920263
weak           0.5840526



#### b. refit model with different priors and compare results
```{r}
fits <- lapply(priors_bin, function(p) {
  stan_surv(formula = Surv(time, status) ~ s_pv_max_pg
            + (1| centre),
            basehaz = "ms",
            data = df,
            prior_intercept = normal(location = 0, scale = 20, autoscale = FALSE),
            prior = p,
            prior_covariance =  decov(regularization = 2, concentration = 1, shape = 1, scale = 1),
            iter    = 2000,
            chains = 4,
            cores = 4,
            adapt_delta = 0.9999,  # Often helpful for complex models
            seed = 666
            )
})
```



#### c. compare posterior intervals for hazard ratios for pg across different priors
```{r}
# calculate median hazard ratio across different priors
HR_med_sens <- sapply(fits, function(f) {
  posterior::as_draws_df(f) |>
    as.data.frame() |>
    summarise(
      median = exp(quantile(s_pv_max_pg, probs = 0.5))
    )
})
HR_med <- c(HR_med_sens[[1]], HR_med_sens[[2]], HR_med_sens[[3]])


# calculate 89% credible interval for hazard ratio across different priors
HR_sens <- sapply(fits, function(f) {
  exp(posterior_interval(f, pars = "s_pv_max_pg", prob = 0.89))
})

# combine median and credible intervals into a summary table
HR_sens_summary <- rbind(HR_med, HR_sens)
row.names(HR_sens_summary) <- c("Median", "Lower", "Upper")

# transpose the table for better readability
HR_sens_summary
```

# X. Bayesian multi-level survival analysis for effect of RIGHT CHF with random intercept for centre

## Set prior for beta variables
Set an informative prior...
 ~ student_t(df = 3, location = 1.57583, scale = 0.7705384)
 
```{r}
prior_beta_chf <- student_t(df = 3, location = c(1.57583, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0),
                            scale = c(0.7705384, 2, 2, 2, 2, 2, 2),
                            autoscale = c(FALSE, FALSE, FALSE, FALSE, TRUE, TRUE, FALSE))
```

Based on the DAG, use the following adjustment variables: RV syst dys, arrhyth, concurrent congen, pressure grad, referral centre, stenosis type




## Fit model
NB use status ... rstanarm requires the dead animals to be classified as 1, whilst censored are 0.
```{r}
mod_chf <- stan_surv(formula = Surv(time, status) ~ chf

                     + type

  prior = prior_beta_chf,
  prior_covariance =  decov(regularization = 2, concentration = 1, shape = 1, scale = 1),
  iter    = 10000,
  chains = 4,
  cores = 4,
  adapt_delta = 0.999,  # Often helpful for complex models
  seed = 666)
```

```{r}
               title = element_text(size=14, face="bold"),
               plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5),
               axis.text.x = element_text(color = "grey50", size = 12),
               axis.text.y = element_text(color = "grey50",size = 12)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 1, linetype="dotted", 
                color = "firebrick", linewidth = 1.5) +
  xlim(0, 2) +
  ylim(0, 3)
```






## Check model performance
### 1. Check performance of posterior probability
NB equivalent of pp_check
```{r}
ps_check(mod_aten_pre) |>
  suppressWarnings()
```



### 2. Check performance of prior probability
```{r}
mod_aten_pre_prior_only <- update(mod_aten_pre, prior_PD = TRUE)
ps_check(mod_aten_pre_prior_only) |>
  suppressWarnings()
```




### 3. Check posterior vs prior for beta variable
#### a. extract draws for posterior and prior
```{r}
# extract draws
post_draws  <- as.matrix(mod_aten_pre)
prior_draws <- as.matrix(mod_aten_pre_prior_only)
```



#### b. plot marginal distributions for posterior and prior
``` {r}
# Compare marginal distributions
dens(post_draws[, "atenolol_pre"], show.zero = TRUE, col = "red", main = "Informed prior vs posterior for initial atenolol", xlab = "Beta coefficient for effect of initial atenolol", xlim = c(-5, 4), ylim = c(0, 0.9))
dens(prior_draws[, "atenolol_pre"], add=TRUE, col = "blue", show.zero = TRUE)
```



#### c. compute prior tail probability of posterior mean
If this probability is very small (e.g. < 0.05), the posterior lies in a region the prior considered implausible.
```{r}
beta_hat <- mean(post_draws[, "atenolol_pre"])

mean(abs(prior_draws[, "atenolol_pre"] - beta_hat) <
       abs(prior_draws[, "atenolol_pre"] - mean(prior_draws[, "atenolol_pre"])))

```





### 4. Sensitivity analyses to assess robustness of results to choice of prior
#### a. create priors of different strength for s_vmaxav_vmaxpv variable
To determine whether the substantive conclusions depend upon the exact prior choice.

NB the scale variable is strengthened or weakened by multiplying or dividing the scale of the main prior by 2, respectively. The location is set to the posterior mean from the main model, to ensure that the priors are centred on a plausible value.
NB.  Had to use 0.5, 1, and 2 to ensure that the chains all completed.
```{r}
priors_bin <- list(
  weak = student_t(df = 3, location = c(1.866284, 0), scale = c(3.3775394, 2), autoscale = c(FALSE, TRUE)),
  moderate = student_t(df = 3, location = c(1.866284, 0), scale = c(1.6887697, 2), autoscale = c(FALSE, TRUE)),
  strong = student_t(df = 3, location = c(1.866284, 0), scale = c(0.8443848, 2), autoscale = c(FALSE, TRUE))
)
```

strong         0.8443848
moderate       1.6887697
weak           3.3775394



#### b. refit model with different priors and compare results
```{r}
fits <- lapply(priors_bin, function(p) {
  stan_surv(formula = Surv(time, status) ~ atenolol_pre
                      + s_tapse
                      + (1| centre),
            basehaz = "ms",
            data = df,
            prior_intercept = normal(location = 0, scale = 20, autoscale = FALSE),
            prior = p,
            prior_covariance =  decov(regularization = 2, concentration = 1, shape = 1, scale = 1),
            iter    = 2000,
            chains = 4,
            cores = 4,
            adapt_delta = 0.99999,  # Often helpful for complex models
            control = list(max_treedepth = 20),
            init = 0.1,
            seed = 666
            )
})
```



#### c. compare posterior intervals for hazard ratios for type_ab across different priors
```{r}
# calculate median hazard ratio across different priors
HR_med_sens <- sapply(fits, function(f) {
  posterior::as_draws_df(f) |>
    as.data.frame() |>
    summarise(
      median = exp(quantile(atenolol_pre, probs = 0.5))
    )
})
HR_med <- c(HR_med_sens[[1]], HR_med_sens[[2]], HR_med_sens[[3]])


# calculate 89% credible interval for hazard ratio across different priors
HR_sens <- sapply(fits, function(f) {
  exp(posterior_interval(f, pars = "atenolol_pre", prob = 0.89))
})

# combine median and credible intervals into a summary table
HR_sens_summary <- rbind(HR_med, HR_sens)
row.names(HR_sens_summary) <- c("Median", "Lower", "Upper")

# transpose the table for better readability
HR_sens_summary
```

# XIIb. Bayesian multi-level survival analysis for effect of ATENOLOL post with random intercept for centre and control set

## Set prior for beta variables
Set an informative prior ...
 ~ student_t(df = 3, location = 1.866284, scale = 0.8443848)
 
```{r}
prior_beta_aten_post <- student_t(df = 3, location = c(1.866284, 0, 0),
                                    scale = c(0.8443848, 2.5, 2.5),
                                    autoscale = c(FALSE, TRUE, FALSE))
```

Based on the DAG, use the following adjustment variables: RV syst dys, aten pre, referral centre (and sx yes).
NB need to use surgery df to ensure that the analysis is only on dogs that have had surgery.



## Fit model
NB use status ... rstanarm requires the dead animals to be classified as 1, whilst censored are 0.
```{r}
mod_aten_post <- stan_surv(formula = Surv(time, status) ~ atenolol_post
                      + s_tapse
                      + atenolol_pre
                      + (1| centre),
  data = df_surg,
  basehaz = "ms",
  prior_intercept = normal(location = 0, scale = 8, autoscale = FALSE),
  prior = prior_beta_aten_post,
  prior_covariance =  decov(regularization = 2, concentration = 1, shape = 1, scale = 1),
  iter    = 14000,
  chains = 4,
  cores = 4,
  adapt_delta = 0.99999,  # Often helpful for complex models
  control = list(max_treedepth = 20),
  init = 0.1,
  seed = 666)
```

```{r}
prior_summary(mod_aten_post)
```


### c. Plot posterior distribution for hazard ratio of clin_si_hi
```{r}
ggplot(data.frame(clin_si_hr), aes(x = clin_si_hr)) +
  geom_density(fill = "lightblue", alpha = 0.7) +
  labs(title = "Posterior distribution of hazard ratio for presence of clinical_signs",
       x = "Hazard Ratio",
       y = "Density") +
  theme_bw() +
           theme(axis.title.y = element_text(size=12, face="bold"), 
               axis.title.x = element_text(size=12, face="bold"),
               title = element_text(size=14, face="bold"),
               plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5),
               axis.text.x = element_text(color = "grey50", size = 12),
               axis.text.y = element_text(color = "grey8",size = 12)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 1, linetype="dotted", 
                color = "firebrick", linewidth = 1.5) +
  xlim(0, 10)
```



## Check model performance
### 1.  Check performance of posterior probability
NB equivalent of pp_check
```{r}
ps_check(mod_clin_si) |>
  suppressWarnings()
```



### 2. Check performance of prior probability
```{r}
mod_clin_si_prior_only <- update(mod_clin_si, prior_PD = TRUE)
ps_check(mod_clin_si_prior_only) |>
  suppressWarnings()
```




### 3. Check prosterior vs prior for beta variable
#### a. extract draws for posterior and prior
```{r}
# extract draws
post_draws  <- as.matrix(mod_clin_si)
prior_draws <- as.matrix(mod_clin_si_prior_only)
```



#### b. plot marginal distributions for posterior and prior
``` {r}
# Compare marginal distributions
dens(post_draws[, "clinical_signs"], show.zero = TRUE, col = "red", main = "Informed prior vs posterior for clinical signs", xlab = "Beta coefficient for effect of clinical signs", xlim = c(-1, 3),ylim = c(0, 2))
dens(prior_draws[, "clinical_signs"], add=TRUE, col = "blue", show.zero = TRUE)
```




#### c. compute prior tail probability of posterior mean
If this probability is very small (e.g. < 0.05), the posterior lies in a region the prior considered implausible.
```{r}
beta_hat <- mean(post_draws[, "clinical_signs"])

mean(abs(prior_draws[, "clinical_signs"] - beta_hat) <
       abs(prior_draws[, "clinical_signs"] - mean(prior_draws[, "clinical_signs"])))

```





### 4. Sensitivity analyses to assess robustness of results to choice of prior
#### a. create priors of different strength for clinical_signs variable
To determine whether the substantive conclusions depend upon the exact prior choice.

NB the scale variable is strengthened or weakened by multiplying or dividing the scale of the main prior by 2, respectively. The location is set to the posterior mean from the main model, to ensure that the priors are centred on a plausible value.
NB.  Had to use 0.5, 1, and 2 to ensure that the chains all completed.
```{r}
priors_bin <- list(
  weak = student_t(df = 3, location = c(1.150538, 0, 0),
                   scale = c(0.9819312 , 2, 2),
                   autoscale = FALSE),
  moderate = student_t(df = 3, location = c(1.150538, 0, 0),
                       scale = c(0.4909656 , 2, 2),
                       autoscale = FALSE),
  strong = student_t(df = 3, location = c(1.150538, 0, 0),
                     scale = c(0.2454828 , 2, 2),
                     autoscale = FALSE)
)
```



strong         0.2454828
moderate       0.4909656
weak           0.9819312



#### b. refit model with different priors and compare results
```{r}
fits <- lapply(priors_bin, function(p) {
  stan_surv(formula = Surv(time, status) ~ clinical_signs
                         + chf
                         + arrhythmias
                         + (1| centre),
            basehaz = "ms",
            data = df,
            prior_intercept = normal(location = 0, scale = 20, autoscale = FALSE),
            prior = p,
            prior_covariance =  decov(regularization = 2, concentration = 1, shape = 1, scale = 1),
            iter    = 2000,
            chains = 4,
            cores = 4,
            adapt_delta = 0.9999,  # Often helpful for complex models
            control = list(max_treedepth = 20),
            init = 0.1,
            seed = 666
            )
})
```




#### c. compare posterior intervals for hazard ratios for clinical signs across different priors
```{r}
# calculate median hazard ratio across different priors
HR_med_sens <- sapply(fits, function(f) {
  posterior::as_draws_df(f) |>
    as.data.frame() |>
    summarise(
      median = exp(quantile(clinical_signs, probs = 0.5))
    )
})
HR_med <- c(HR_med_sens[[1]], HR_med_sens[[2]], HR_med_sens[[3]])


# calculate 89% credible interval for hazard ratio across different priors
HR_sens <- sapply(fits, function(f) {
  exp(posterior_interval(f, pars = "clinical_signs", prob = 0.89))
})

# combine median and credible intervals into a summary table
HR_sens_summary <- rbind(HR_med, HR_sens)
row.names(HR_sens_summary) <- c("Median", "Lower", "Upper")

# transpose the table for better readability
HR_sens_summary
```








## Make model predictions and plot for mod_clin_si
### 1. Create new data where complications differs
```{r}
nd <- data.frame(centre = rep("p", 2),
                 clinical_signs = c(0, 1),
                 chf = rep(0, 2),
                 arrhythmias = rep(0, 2)
                 )
head(nd)
```



### 2. Make posterior predictions from new data
```{r}
ps <- posterior_survfit(mod_clin_si,
  newdata = nd,
  times = 0,
  extrapolate = TRUE) |>
  suppressWarnings()
head(ps)
```



### 3. Plot
```{r}
panel_labels <- c('1' = "Clinical signs absent", '2' = "Clinical signs present")
pps <- plot(ps) +
  aes(colour = factor(id), fill = factor(id)) +
  theme(legend.position = "none") +
  facet_wrap(~ id, labeller = labeller(id = panel_labels)) +
           theme(axis.title.y = element_text(size=12, face="bold"), 
               axis.title.x = element_text(size=12, face="bold"),
               title = element_text(size=12, face="bold"),
               plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5),
               axis.text.x = element_text(color = "grey50", size = 10),
               axis.text.y = element_text(color = "grey50",size = 10)) +
            theme(strip.text.x = element_text(size = 10, face = "bold.italic"),
                   strip.background = element_rect(fill="white")
        )

print(pps)
```



## Check PH assumption visually
### make predictions of both the hazard and log hazard
```{r}
ph <- suppressWarnings( posterior_survfit(mod_clin_si, newdata = nd, type = "haz") )
pl <- suppressWarnings( posterior_survfit(mod_clin_si, newdata = nd, type = "loghaz") )
```



#### create plots
```{r}
pph <- plot(ph) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0.0, 0.005)) +
  facet_wrap(~ id, labeller = labeller(id = panel_labels))
ppl <- plot(pl) +
  facet_wrap(~ id, labeller = labeller(id = panel_labels))
```



#### combine plots in grid and plot
```{r, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 8}
plot_grid(pph, ppl, ncol = 1)
```
